answer: Meter the power behind each agent. Its host streams readings from a utility-signed smart meter, and the network grants one seat per distinct meter whose draw rises and falls with that agent's own workload. A farm running 400 clones from one rack in a canyon-side data center shows a single sable, flat load curve instead of 400 separate plumes of compute spikes, so its clones collapse into one seat. Faking it means renting 400 separately metered sites at about $30 a month each, roughly $12,000 monthly.
